# Startup Studio

> A shared team of seventeen AI agents for a solo founder who cannot afford a team. It is an
> open source multi-agent framework: one roster of roles, layered per project, with rules the
> tooling refuses to break rather than rules somebody is trusted to remember.

Startup Studio runs on Claude Code today. That is a limitation of this tooling and not of the
method: the roster installs into the directories one specific coding agent reads, and the two
hooks are registered that agent's way.

What makes it different from a prompt pack is that several rules are enforced by the software
rather than written down. Only the QA role can move a ticket to user acceptance testing, and
only with test notes written first. Nothing is released without a changelog entry. A ticket
cannot be closed over a question nobody answered. A large piece of work cannot start until an
assessment carrying a verdict and a measure is recorded against it.

The front door itself is the method rather than the software: six leads argue a large idea from
their own disciplines before it is built, and a verdict of no is a normal outcome. What the
board enforces is that the record exists, which is the only part a program can honestly check.

## Pages

- [Home](https://startupstudio.projectfreedom.xyz/): what the studio is, in the founder's own words, and who it is for.
- [The problem](https://startupstudio.projectfreedom.xyz/problem): why building got fast and knowing whether it mattered got harder.
- [The solution](https://startupstudio.projectfreedom.xyz/solution): the seventeen roles, what each owns, and the four points where the founder decides.
- [Prototypes](https://startupstudio.projectfreedom.xyz/prototypes): five products and this studio, built by the one team, in domains with nothing in common.
- [How to run it](https://startupstudio.projectfreedom.xyz/how-to): install once, tune only what differs, and ship.
- [Release notes](https://startupstudio.projectfreedom.xyz/releases): every release, newest first, generated from the changelog.
- [Reference](https://startupstudio.projectfreedom.xyz/reference): the board and its eight columns, the stack with the reason for each choice, every command the tool takes, and a nineteen-term glossary where every term has its own address.

## Source

- [Repository](https://github.com/creationisttest-git/startup_studio): AGPL-3.0, the full roster, the board and the tooling.
